opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ian Johnson (employee ID E028) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E028.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Ian Johnson (E028) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As the role owns the Payroll system, admin access is within policy for this employee.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E028 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can only have read (or write with advanced training); they are never allowed admin. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: The Security agent's note (from the Security DB) identifies E028 as a contractor with basic security training. Under the access policy, contractors may have at most read (write only with advanced training) and are never allowed admin. The requested admin level exceeds the maximum for a contractor, so the maximum of read is granted. (Note: HR's record lists E028 as a full-time Payroll Specialist, which conflicts; granting beyond read would risk violating the contractor policy, so I apply the more restrictive, policy-compliant level.)
